title: Simple circuits
description: Close a battery, a wire, and a bulb into one loop, then see how the bulb responds to the voltage.
learningObjectives: Explain that a bulb lights when the path out of the battery and back is closed
Predict that a higher voltage makes this bulb brighter

params.description: Battery voltage in volts. A higher value makes this bulb brighter.

events.name: component_connected
events.description: The child connected a part and closed the loop.

events.name: bulb_lit
events.description: The bulb lit at the battery voltage.

tutorGuide.intro: This battery, wire, and bulb make a circuit only when the path is a closed loop. Connect the battery and watch the bulb respond to the voltage.
steps: Look at the battery, the wire, and the bulb, and notice the open gap.
Predict whether the bulb will light when that gap closes.
Connect the battery lead and compare the glow with the voltage.
observationPrompts: What changed in the path when you connected the battery?
How bright is the filament at this voltage, and what would you expect if the voltage were higher?

misconceptions.belief: The electricity is used up in the bulb, so nothing returns to the battery.
misconceptions.response: Charge keeps moving around the closed loop. The bulb turns some energy into light and heat, and the path still comes back to the battery.

misconceptions.belief: One wire from the battery is enough to light the bulb.
misconceptions.response: The path has to leave the battery and come back. An open gap means no current, so the bulb stays dark.

hints: Find the battery. The loop is still open at its lead.
Connect the battery lead so the wire meets both ends of the path.
A closed loop lets the bulb light. The voltage is the push from the battery.

successCriteria.description: Connected the battery so the loop closed
Saw the bulb light at the given voltage

accessibility.screenReaderSummary: A battery, a wire, and a bulb. Connect the battery lead to close the loop. The bulb lights, and the voltage is shown.
